newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic only candidate for Yugoslav presidency.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic only candidate for Yugoslav presidency.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic will be the only candidate for the Yugoslavia presidency when the post is filled this month, federal parliament committees decided on Monday.
He is expected to be elected despite tensions with the leadership of the ruling DPS party in the republic of Montenegro, Serbia's partner in the Yugoslav federation.
The DPS said it would vote for Milosevic but would not allow him to change the federal constitution to give the ceremonial federal presidency more authority.
Milosevic was nominated by his ruling Socialist party (SPS) for the federal presidency because he is prevented by the constitution from seeking a third term as president of Serbia.
Despite the federal job's limited official powers, he is expected to remain the dominant political force in Yugoslavia through SPS control of the security apparatus, economy and police.
The federal parliament will elect Milosevic by July 25 and elections for the Serbian presidency will follow within 60 days.
With opposition parties in disarray despite being joined in a nominal coalition, the Socialists are expected to retain Serbia's presidency with a nominee loyal to Milosevic.
